core_philosophy.mission: Acquire language naturally, not just learn it. Methods based on first-language acquisition: comprehensible input, observation, repetition, play.

dual_mission.statement: Classes are English AND AI — the two highest-leverage skills for career advancement in Vietnam
quotes: These weren't just meant to be English classes. They're meant to be English and AI.
AI is more important than English for your career and making money in the next couple years. It might already be more important than English.

three_mistakes_of_vietnamese_education.traditional: Memorize large amounts of words not useful in everyday life
three_mistakes_of_vietnamese_education.net_fix: Focus only on high-frequency practical words students actually use

three_mistakes_of_vietnamese_education.traditional: Learn a word once and move on
three_mistakes_of_vietnamese_education.net_fix: Systematic review through AI-powered spaced repetition
University-proven spaced repetition intervals that defeat forgetting curve

net_mindset: Acquire, don't just learn — mirror first-language acquisition
Graduate, don't retain — set students up for independence after one year
Quality over quantity — know fewer words deeply, use them in many ways
Daily commitment non-negotiable — 1 hour of English every day
Fun is not optional, it's science — brain learns faster when engaged
Passion drives acquisition — connect English to what students already love
core_philosophy.passion_proof: 8-year-old who couldn't speak English was speaking full sentences after one year — lessons focused on chess, Free Fire, and Roblox

pillar_1_learn_like_native.principle: Natural acquisition over grammar drilling. Listening and mimicking over rote memorization.

pillar_2_comprehensible_input.rule: 60% Rule — student must understand at least 60% of what they're listening to

zones.60_to_80: SWEET SPOT — natural acquisition, brain fills gaps from context
zones.above_90: Too easy — no growth, brain disengages

pillar_2_comprehensible_input.daily_practice: 45 min listening to content student enjoys

pillar_4_spaced_repetition.quote: You will repeat and be reminded of new words often — maybe every day for a week or two, then a couple times a week, then once a month, then once every 3 months, and then it is permanently your word.
pillar_4_spaced_repetition.ai_integration: Students log Key Struggle Points daily. AI learns what to review and re-introduces at optimal intervals.

mouse_to_tiger.framework: Central metaphor and behavioral framework. Every student enters as Mouse, graduates as Tiger.

transformation_phases.name: Mastery
transformation_phases.focus: Tiger is default, Mouse is gone

intervention_scripts: You're using Mouse Voice right now

cub.indicators: Attempting output, reducing I don't know, growing volume

tiger.indicators: Confident, unapologetic, thinks in English, approaches foreigners

confidence_first_sequence.quote: My first thing is to work on your confidence. It's not even about the English at the beginning.
confidence_first_sequence.rule: English acquisition accelerates AFTER confidence foundation is set

feedback_sandwich: Praise: Great job speaking for 30 seconds!

three_metaphors.elephant_in_chains: Vietnamese students told don't speak until perfect. Invisible chains. NET breaks them.
three_metaphors.grammar_prison: Traditional education locks students in rules, shames mistakes. NET is the escape key.
three_metaphors.phoenix_rebirth: Learning English is a rebirth. Old scared self burns away. New confident speaker emerges.

confidence_algorithm.mirroring_technique: Teacher says phrase, student repeats with confidence. Focus on projection and clarity. No translation.

energy_management.rule: adjust pace and activities in real time

classroom_techniques.pair_practice: Students drill in pairs — peer support before full-class performance

value_stack.buddy_system: Every student paired for weekly conversational practice. Builds peer accountability, friendships, network.

advanced_techniques.name: Anchor Principle
advanced_techniques.method: Find one word student CAN pronounce correctly, use as anchor. Return to anchor when student drifts.
advanced_techniques.origin: Gemini phonics session with Denny Nguyen

advanced_techniques.name: ABC Eyes-Closed Practice
advanced_techniques.method: Student closes eyes, recites sounds. Removes visual self-consciousness, forces focus on mouth position.

advanced_techniques.name: 3-Tries Rule
advanced_techniques.method: Exactly 3 attempts before teacher models correct version. Not 1 (too harsh), not unlimited (builds frustration).

advanced_techniques.name: 3-Week Build / 3-Month Destroy
advanced_techniques.method: 3 weeks consistent practice = new habit. 3 months neglect = old pattern re-cements.
advanced_techniques.application: Maintain correction pressure for full 3-week cycle

advanced_techniques.name: I Don't Know Breakthrough
advanced_techniques.method: Redirect 'I don't know' to 'Try. Say something.' Moment student stops defaulting = Mouse → Cub transition marker.

advanced_techniques.name: 30% Slower Challenge
advanced_techniques.method: Ask student to speak at 70% speed. Forces clarity, reduces filler words, reveals higher actual ability.
advanced_techniques.best_for: CUB level with vocabulary but poor clarity

advanced_techniques.name: Genre-Based Vocabulary Hooks
advanced_techniques.method: Build vocabulary from student's passion domain instead of generic lists.

examples.horror_fan: thriller, suspense, creepy, haunted, plot twist

favorite_topic.law: Every human's #1 favorite topic is themselves
favorite_topic.teaching_method: Present as riddle with 100,000 VND reward. Common wrong answers: money, culture, food.
favorite_topic.application: Get good at asking questions about them → they love you → they don't notice your English level

follow_up_questions.definition: Asking more specific questions based on what someone just told you — go deeper instead of pivoting to yourself
follow_up_questions.wrong_move: Someone says 'I love music' → 'Oh yeah, I play guitar too. Me me me.'
follow_up_questions.right_move: Someone says 'I love music' → 'What instruments do you play?' → 'How long?' → 'Which do you like better?' → 'Why?'
follow_up_questions.power_word: Why — the single most powerful word for keeping conversations going

conversation_principles.professional_opener: 'What do you do?' = universal English opener for professional contexts. Means 'What is your job?'
conversation_principles.confidence_bypass: For shy/introvert students: learn to ask questions → takes pressure off → you control conversation → they do most talking

vietnamese_specific.listening_habit: Vietnamese students focus on what they DON'T know instead of what they DO know. 95% of words are known — the 5% unknown should never stop the flow.
vietnamese_specific.listening_trap: Hear unknown word → STOP LISTENING → Focus on unknown → Miss entire message
vietnamese_specific.flow_of_context: Hear unknown word → KEEP LISTENING → Use context clues → Understand message

gemini_as_teaching_tool.method: Google Gemini voice mode as real-time Vietnamese-English bridge during beginner classes
commands: Translate that directly to Vietnamese, no commentary
Tell them in Vietnamese the four things
Use English and Vietnamese like a hybrid
gemini_as_teaching_tool.limitations: Sometimes adds unnecessary commentary, switches languages, refuses certain vocabulary

phone_consequences.rule: No phones during class. Phone visible = consequence.
phone_consequences.philosophy: Consequences are fun not punitive — each forces performance in English. Escalation doubles if student refuses.

brain_rot_teaching.core: Social media activates same brain chemicals as drugs/alcohol/gambling
brain_rot_teaching.teaching_angle: Not just health lecture — vocabulary building (addicted, stressful, doom scrolling) woven into real conversation

metaphors.chinese_bamboo_tree: No visible growth for years while building roots. Then explosive growth. Reassures students first 3 months of confidence-building IS progress.
metaphors.sharpen_your_axe: Keep chopping without sharpening → axe breaks. Work-life balance. Don't drive yourself too hard or you'll get sick.

classroom_to_curriculum: Pheromone trail: FAILURE → ROOT CAUSE → FIX → VERIFY
